Plot p-value curves over a continuous perturbation

Source: R/plots.R
plot_pcurve.Rd

Draws the p-value against the parameter for every family of rows that carries a param value (from stress_tipping() or stress_curve()): one line per family, the alpha reference line, the anchor point (the row of kind = "alternative", usually the unshifted analysis) emphasised, and a dotted vertical line at each interpolated crossing with its value.

Usage

plot_pcurve(
  rows,
  alpha = NULL,
  xlab = "Perturbation",
  ylab = "p-value",
  log_p = FALSE
)

Arguments

rows

A stress_rows data frame or stress_census; rows without a param are ignored.

alpha

Significance level; defaults to the rows' own alpha.

xlab, ylab

Axis labels.

log_p

Draw the p-value axis on a log scale.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

small <- mmrm::fev_data[mmrm::fev_data$USUBJID %in% paste0("PT", 1:80), ]
spec <- stress_spec(small, "FEV1", "USUBJID", "AVISIT", "ARMCD", "PBO", covariates = ~ FEV1_BL)
tp <- stress_tipping(spec, deltas = c(0, -4, -8), m = 3)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) plot_pcurve(tp)
